summary.text: Kathleen Williams is the Democratic candidate for Montana State Senate District 31 in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing Republican Richard Aungier for a seat with no incumbent.

A former member of the Montana House of Representatives who served from 2011 to 2017 and the Democratic nominee for Montana’s at-large U.S. House seat in 2018 and 2020, she has worked on water and natural resources issues.

paragraphs.text: Kathleen Williams earned a B.S. in Resource Economics from the University of California, Berkeley, in 1983 and an M.S. in Recreation Resources from Colorado State University in 1990.

Her professional experience, as Ballotpedia lists it, includes work as executive director of the Instream Flow Council, water resources program manager at the Montana Department of Fish, Wildlife & Parks, research analyst at the Legislative Environmental Policy Office of the Montana Legislature, conservation planner at Oregon Trout, and river and recreation planner at the U.S. Forest Service.
Williams represented Montana House of Representatives District 61 from 2011 to 2017.
She was the Democratic nominee for the U.S. House in Montana’s at-large district in 2018, losing to incumbent Greg Gianforte, and again in 2020, losing to Matt Rosendale.
She advanced from the Democratic primary for Senate District 31 on June 2, 2026.

In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, Williams said her priorities include affordability, including housing, food and childcare costs; fair tax policy; public education; the state’s energy future; and the protection of Montana’s outdoor heritage.
